title: Ginzan Onsen snowy night instead of Zao
summary: Take the Yamagata Shinkansen to Oishida and see the old wooden ryokan street of Ginzan Onsen in snow and gas-lamp light at dusk. Stay the night in Tendo Onsen or Obanazawa, then Yamadera in the morning and Sendai gyutan in the evening.
why: It is the most famous snow night view in Tohoku (the 'Spirited Away' look that is huge on Xiaohongshu), and it keeps the onsen night without the ski day that is hard for Aoki.
cost: Tokyo–Oishida Shinkansen ~12,000 JPY one way; Ginzan shuttle 1,000–1,500 JPY; Tendo night tour 9,800 JPY; ryokan in Tendo 15,000–30,000 JPY with dinner
winterNote: Winter 2026–27 (Dec 2026–early Mar 2027): no private cars; day visitors park at Taisho Roman-kan and ride a timed shuttle (9:00–18:00, 1,000–1,500 JPY, stay about 1 h 20 min). Advance booking strongly recommended, same-day slots very few. Day visitors not allowed about 20:00–10:00. Easiest: Tendo Onsen 'Twilight Trip' tour, 12 Dec 2026–14 Mar 2027, 15:15 from Tendo, back ~19:15, 9,800 JPY incl. entry + fast pass. Ryokan rooms in Ginzan itself sell out very early.

title: Yamadera mountain temple in snow
summary: Climb about 1,000 stone steps through snowy cedar forest to temple halls on a cliff with a wide view of the valley. It is on the Senzan Line between Yamagata (20 min) and Sendai (about 1 h).
why: It fits the day 7 move from Zao/Yamagata to Sendai with no extra travel, and the snow view from Godaido is a classic Tohoku photo.
cost: Entry ~300 JPY; train Yamagata–Yamadera ~240 JPY, Yamadera–Sendai ~860 JPY
winterNote: Temple is open in winter but steps can be icy; wear shoes with grip or bring slip-on spikes. Some upper halls may close in bad weather. Opening hours in winter are shorter (check on site).

title: Aomori and Hakkoda instead of Sendai
summary: After Zao on day 7, go north to Aomori (Sendai–Shin-Aomori about 1 h 30 min) for the Nebuta Museum and seafood. On day 8 take the bus to Hakkoda Ropeway for snow monsters and a Sukayu onsen bath, then a 1 h Shinkansen to Hakodate.
why: It shortens the long day 8 Hayabusa ride, gives a second, bigger snow-monster field, and Pegasis can ski Hakkoda's famous deep powder.
cost: Bus Aomori–ropeway 1,290 JPY one way; ropeway round trip ~2,500 JPY; Sukayu bath ~1,000 JPY; Nebuta Museum ~620 JPY
winterNote: Ropeway winter hours 9:00–15:40, stops in strong wind. JR Bus from Aomori Station runs only to Sukayu in winter (road beyond closed), ~80 min. Snow monsters are best Jan–Feb. Hakkoda is mostly ungroomed off-piste terrain: fine for Pegasis (a guide is advised off the course), not good for a beginner (Aoki can do snowshoe tour instead).

places.ja: ねぶたの家 ワ・ラッセ

title: Sukayu Onsen giant wooden bath
summary: A very old mountain onsen with the huge 'Sen-nin buro' wooden bath hall, milky acidic water, under some of the deepest snow in Japan. You can bathe as a day visitor or stay one night.
why: It is one of the most famous onsen in Japan, and the walls of snow around it look unreal in late January.
winterNote: Open all winter; bus from Aomori Station ~70 min. The big bath is mixed (konyoku) with a women-only time slot; small separate baths also exist. Check women-only hours before you go.

title: Oirase Gorge frozen waterfalls tour
titleJa: 奥入瀬渓流 氷瀑ツアー
summary: A guided bus and walk tour to the frozen waterfalls and ice pillars along the Oirase stream, with a night tour that lights up five ice falls. Best done with a night at the Oirase Keiryu Onsen area.
why: Blue-white ice falls lit at night are a rare winter sight, and it pairs well with an Aomori swap.
winterNote: 2025–26 ran 20 Dec–1 Mar, only Fri/Sat/Sun and New Year. In 2027, day 6 (Sun 24 Jan) fits; days 7–8 (Mon/Tue) do not. Meeting point depends on the course (Towada city, Oirase Keiryu Onsen, or Lake Towada for night tour); booking at frozen-oirase.com. Getting there without a car needs a hotel shuttle (e.g. from Hachinohe/Shin-Aomori) — check.

title: Stove train and snowy Hirosaki Castle
titleJa: 津軽鉄道ストーブ列車・弘前城
summary: Ride the Tsugaru Railway stove train from Tsugaru-Goshogawara, where staff grill dried squid on a coal stove, and see the tall Tachineputa floats and Dazai Osamu's house in Kanagi. In the afternoon walk Hirosaki Castle park in snow, then take the Shinkansen from Shin-Aomori to Hakodate.
why: It is a slow, local, very 'Showa' winter day with a unique train, a good contrast to ski days, and needs no driving.
duration: 1 day (needs night 7 in Aomori or Hirosaki)
cost: Stove train surcharge 1,000 JPY + fare; JR Aomori–Goshogawara/Hirosaki ~1,000–1,500 JPY; Tachineputa museum ~650 JPY
winterNote: Stove train runs 1 Dec 2026–31 Mar 2027, 3 round trips a day (times can change; tel 0173-34-2148). Hirosaki Castle Snow Lantern Festival is early Feb (2026: 6–11 Feb), so it is after this trip. Aomori–Goshogawara by JR is about 1 h+, Hirosaki–Shin-Aomori about 35 min.

title: Kakunodate, Nyuto, Hakkoda rail loop
titleJa: 角館・乳頭温泉郷・八甲田
summary: Replace Zao and Sendai with a northern route: Tokyo to Kakunodate samurai street by Komachi (about 3 h), then bus to Nyuto Onsen for a night at a snowbound old inn. Next day Morioka (wanko soba) and on to Aomori or Sukayu, and on day 8 Hakkoda snow monsters before the 1 h train to Hakodate.
why: It gives the two most famous snowy onsen in north Japan and a second snow-monster field, all by train, and cuts the day 8 ride to Hokkaido to 1 h.
cost: Rail Tokyo–Kakunodate ~17,000 JPY; Nyuto inn 15,000–25,000 JPY with meals; Tazawako–Nyuto bus ~900 JPY; Tsurunoyu day bath ~700–800 JPY
winterNote: Nyuto: bus from Tazawako Station ~45 min; Tsurunoyu is reached by its own pick-up from Alpa Komakusa (booking needed). Tsurunoyu day bathing 10:00–15:00, outdoor bath closed on Mondays (day 7 = Mon 25 Jan 2027). Tsurunoyu rooms are hard to book; other Nyuto inns (Kyukamura, Taenoyu, Kuroyu may close in winter — check). Kakunodate and Yokote Kamakura festivals are mid-Feb, after the trip.

title: Appi Kogen ski instead of Zao
summary: Ski at Appi Kogen in Iwate, a big resort with dry snow, long groomed runs and good ski school, about 1 h by bus from Morioka. Then continue north on day 8 from Morioka on the Hayabusa.
why: It is better than Zao for a beginner like Aoki (wide gentle runs, lessons in English), still fun for Pegasis, and it is on the way to Hokkaido.
cost: Lift 1 day ~7,000–8,000 JPY; rental ~6,000 JPY; hotel 12,000–25,000 JPY; Tokyo–Morioka ~15,000 JPY
winterNote: Peak snow season in late January. Shuttle from Morioka Station to the resort; confirm 2026–27 times and if it is only for hotel guests. You lose the Zao snow monsters and Sendai gyutan (gyutan can be a station lunch box).

title: Morioka wanko soba lunch stop
summary: Break the day 8 Hayabusa ride at Morioka for wanko soba, where staff keep refilling small bowls of soba until you close the lid. Most people eat 50–100 bowls; add Morioka reimen if still hungry.
why: It is a fun eating challenge that both can do together, and Morioka is a Hayabusa stop so it costs only about 2 h.
winterNote: Open all year. Use the same rail ticket; take a later Hayabusa from Morioka (Morioka–Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto about 2 h). Busy at weekend lunch; day 8 is a Tuesday.

title: Matsushima bay or Hiraizumi temples
titleJa: 松島・平泉 中尊寺
summary: From Sendai, Matsushima bay with its pine islands and Zuiganji temple is 40 min on the Senseki Line. Or on day 8 stop at Ichinoseki for Hiraizumi's golden hall Chusonji (UNESCO), then take a later train north.
why: Easy culture and scenery near the baseline route for a slow half day after skiing; Matsushima also has fresh winter oysters.
cost: Chusonji ~1,000 JPY; Zuiganji ~700 JPY; Matsushima boat ~1,500 JPY; local trains ~400–600 JPY
winterNote: Both open in winter. Hiraizumi: Tohoku Shinkansen Sendai–Ichinoseki ~30 min (Yamabiko), then JR 8 min to Hiraizumi; most Hayabusa do not stop at Ichinoseki, so change at Sendai or Morioka.

title: Aizu castle and Ouchi-juku in snow
summary: Go to Aizu-Wakamatsu (via Koriyama, about 2 h 40 min from Tokyo) for Tsuruga Castle in snow, then Ouchi-juku, a street of thatched-roof Edo inns buried in snow. Train fans can add a ride on the snowy Tadami Line to the First Tadami River Bridge viewpoint.
why: Samurai history and a thatched snow village are strong 'old Japan' images, different from ski resorts.
cost: Tokyo–Aizu ~9,000 JPY; castle ~410 JPY; Ouchi-juku taxi from Yunokami-Onsen station ~2,000–3,000 JPY per car
winterNote: Ouchi-juku Snow Festival is 2nd weekend of Feb (2026: 14–15 Feb), after this trip, but the village is snowy all of late Jan. Tadami Line has only a few trains a day (Aizu-Wakamatsu–Koide about 4.5 h); plan carefully, snow can stop trains. Day 7 returns to Sendai via Koriyama (~2 h). Replaces Zao ski.

title: North Tohoku winter road trip
titleJa: 東北 冬ドライブ（盛岡〜青森）
summary: Aoki drives a 4WD rental with snow tyres from Morioka: Appi or Hachimantai, Nyuto Onsen, Lake Towada and Oirase, then over the Hakkoda snow walls to Sukayu and Aomori. Drop the car at Shin-Aomori and take the Shinkansen to Hakodate.
why: Aoki gets real snow driving, and the car reaches Oirase, Towada and Nyuto, which are slow by bus in winter.
cost: 4WD compact ~10,000–15,000 JPY/day + one-way drop fee (Morioka→Aomori, often several thousand JPY) + fuel
winterNote: Mountain roads in heavy snow and possible whiteouts; drive only in daylight. Hachimantai Aspite Line and the Towada–Hakkoda road beyond Sukayu (N103/N394 sections) close in winter; use open routes only and check road info (JARTIC) the day before. Pegasis cannot share driving. Towada winter festival (2026: 30 Jan–23 Feb, closed Tue–Thu) starts after these dates.

title: Lake Towada Winter Story festival
summary: Snow sculptures, ice bars, light-up and small winter fireworks at 20:00 by Lake Towada at Yasumiya. It is one of the 'five snow festivals of Michinoku'.
why: Only relevant if the trip is moved later; it is a nice night event with a winter onsen stay.
winterNote: 2026 dates: 30 Jan–23 Feb, closed Tue–Thu, 16:00–20:30 (weekends 11:00–21:00). 2027 dates not yet announced, but it starts about late Jan, when the baseline is already in Hokkaido. Same for Hirosaki Snow Lantern (early Feb), Ouchi-juku (mid Feb), Yokote Kamakura (15–16 Feb).
